public_rationale: The available research documents cloud concentration, but does not trace AI-product spending through suppliers. A 67% cloud revenue share cannot be compared directly with a claim that some portion of nearly every AI purchase reaches big tech. Neither support nor contradiction is established.
limitations: The available market data cover cloud infrastructure generally.
The claim's accounting basis is unknown, preventing a supported or contradicted money assessment.
Individual supplier agreements would not establish the sector-wide proportion.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Almost every dollar spent on AI products is eventually shared with a few multi-trillion-dollar tech firms.

statement.excerpt: Big tech has turned the startup ecosystem into a giant goldmine, one that guarantees that almost every dollar spent on any AI product is eventually shared with one of a few multi-trillion dollar tech firms.

from_speaker: almost every dollar spent on any AI product
one of a few multi-trillion dollar tech firms
our_interpretation: Read shared as some portion of nearly all AI-product spending reaching a major technology supplier through direct or indirect payments; the claim does not say suppliers retain the entire dollar.
The surrounding discussion identifies Amazon, Microsoft, and Google as the relevant supplier group.
Assess the existing payment structure using the latest completed quarter before publication, October through December 2023; the preceding paragraph also refers to the last quarter.
Eventually refers to the supplier payment chain, not a forecast with a future deadline.
No accounting basis is supplied for the asserted spending coverage, so accounting_basis is unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Representative payment-chain data show that nearly all AI-product expenditure generates some attributable supplier revenue for the identified technology firms, with only negligible exceptions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable payment-chain data show a material share of AI-product expenditure whose attributable supplier payments do not reach those firms.

evidence.explanation: The release establishes substantial concentration in cloud infrastructure services during Q4 2023. Its 67% figure neither proves nor disproves nearly universal AI-product payment coverage because the market and payment measure differ.
